page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.large is an entry-level general purpose virtual server based on the 64-bit Arm architecture and hosted on KVM hypervisors. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs backed by an Ampere Altra processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. Memory allocation is set at 8.0 GB, providing 4.0 GB per core to maintain a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory profile. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached cloud disks for persistent filesystem volumes. Hardware acceleration is absent, with 0 GPUs installed, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate compute and memory performance tailored to lightweight operational requirements. In raw CPU testing, the Ampere Altra cores achieve a median stress-ng single-core score of 1790.19, but multi-core throughput registers at 3551.69, falling into lower relative tiers due to the dual-vCPU ceiling. Geekbench scores show 1065.0 for single-core and 1945.0 for multi-core execution. Memory bandwidth metrics yield 24.55 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 15.62 GB/sec for writes on 256 MB blocks. Application tests demonstrate 2.69 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.62 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.g6r.large lies between its cost-efficient Arm core density and restricted aggregate throughput. While the dedicated Ampere cores prevent noisy-neighbor contention, the absence of local storage and a 1 Gbps network baseline constrain I/O-intensive operations. The instance is suited for lightweight microservices, internal staging and development environments, low-traffic web applications, basic Redis caching tiers, and background job consumers that do not require x86-specific instruction sets.
